items.title: Earl Turbinton Interview, 1990-09-01
items.q: I think Alvin had gone to start his program at Southern, so we weren't hearing much of him here.

ctx.x: Can you address a little bit about what do you think the forces were that led to the closure? I mean, I know you said there were lots of other problems, but were there any other things that you think led to the closure?

Just economics. Had we been able to sustain ourselves as well? See, that was a period, as I said, where, say, from 64 up to that period, even for New Orleans, I mean, this was a period that we were making upward of, say, $350 to $500 a week per person and better sometimes, which is, many times musicians don't make, on a local level, they aren't doing it well here now in the 90s or late 80s that wasn't happening. The group was very popular. We were able to get some very good bookings, and we were recognized as…
And the workshop did bear fruit. The workshop did bear fruit.
